title: Harness Engineering: Building the Production Cage for Powerful Domain Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS
talk_summary: Mike Chambers defines a harness as everything in an agent except the model and argues production harnesses must separate loop, memory, runtime, identity, tools, and observability so they scale independently. The demo is mostly AWS Bedrock AgentCore/Strands, showing CLI-generated agents, managed memory, traces, and IaC deployment rather than measured results.

takeaways.technique: Split harness components for independent scaling
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat the agent loop, memory, runtime, identity, tools, and observability as separate deployable components rather than one container, so each can scale independently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: take things like memory and deploy that separately so it can scale separately. taking our loop out so it can scale separately

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a session manager to persist conversation state between invocations and rehydrate history, with long-term memories stored separately.
takeaways.evidence_quote: session manager is helping me to maintain session state between invocations... rehydrate the conversation history

takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument deployed agents to inspect traces and stored memory, and treat observability/evaluations as first-class harness components.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Observability and evaluations super super important.

takeaways.what_they_do: Push multi-tenant isolation into the runtime layer so agent code does not implement tenancy itself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: scale this agent out at runtime and do multi-tenant isolation... without you having to write all the multi-tenented code

takeaways.what_they_do: Define simple agents as JSON config with model and system prompt plus MCP tools, reserving custom code for cases that need it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 80% of agent development is kind of solved already... system prompt connect to some MCP tools

takeaways.what_they_do: Have agents generate infrastructure-as-code rather than directly clicking/creating cloud resources, preserving owned, reviewable deployments.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We want the agent to build up our infrastructure as code... so that we still own our deployments
